literal: If it is said that ruin comes by benevolence, that ruin is a worthy thing to buy even by a person selling himself.
translation: If ruin is said to come from practicing benevolence, such ruin is worth acquiring even by selling oneself.
modern: பிறருக்கு உதவி செய்வதனால் ஒருவனுக்கு அழிவு வரும் என்றால், அந்த அழிவை ஒருவன் தன்னை விற்றாவது வாங்கிக் கொள்ளும் தகுதி உடையதாகும்.
explanation: This couplet praises the supreme virtue of social benevolence (oppuravu). The poet states that even if helping others leads to one's own financial ruin or destruction, that ruin is not a loss to be feared. Instead, it is so glorious and noble that a person should be willing to sell themselves into slavery to purchase such a ruin. The words 'vittu' (selling) and 'kol' (buying) frame this ultimate sacrifice as a highly profitable moral transaction.
